reason: E2 demonstrates glass-to-glass transitions with enhanced thermal stability in a different high-entropy metallic glass, supporting the concept. E1 confirms the target alloy can be made fully amorphous by melt-spinning at the specified cooling rates. However, no cited evidence supports the specific claim that a subcritical thermal pulse relaxes stresses and eliminates nuclei in this alloy, nor the predicted 50 K increase in crystallization onset; these are extrapolations without direct prior data.
premises: A glass-to-glass transition can occur in high-entropy metallic glasses upon heating, releasing significant heat and improving thermal stability.
The Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy can be produced in a fully amorphous state by melt-spinning at 10^5–10^6 K/s.
A subcritical thermal pulse below the crystallization onset can relax internal stresses and eliminate nucleation sites without causing crystallization.
The thermal pulse will increase the crystallization onset temperature by roughly 50 K relative to the as-quenched state.
